question: Does Stellar execute smart-contract transactions in parallel, and when did that capability ship?

golden.answer: Yes—Stellar now applies non-conflicting smart-contract transactions in bounded parallel clusters. **Protocol 23/Whisk** introduced CAP-0063 scheduling support on 2025-09-03, but initialized `ledgerMaxDependentTxClusters` to **1** (no multi-cluster parallel execution). Later network-settings votes raised it to **2** on **2026-01-29 at 17:00 UTC** (SLP-0004, ledger 60993066) and to **3** on **2026-10-22 at 17:00 UTC** (SLP-0007, ledger 65080525). As of 2026-11-02, three independent Mainnet RPC reads decoded setting 3; validators can change this setting again. The scheduler groups disjoint read/write footprints within bounded budgets. This is parallel scheduling, not sharding or a claim that all transactions run concurrently.
keyFacts: Explains non-conflicting/disjoint footprints and current bounded setting.
avoid: Do NOT attribute CAP-0063 to another protocol or call it sharding.
Do NOT say P23 transition itself immediately enabled multiple dependent clusters or that all transactions execute concurrently.
golden.notes:
Parallel execution = CAP-0063 = Protocol 23 Whisk. DATE CORRECTED to 2025-09-03 (was 2025-06-10 in draft — that was the blog publish date, not activation). Verified via stellar.org 'Introducing Whisk' + Protocol 23 Upgrade Guide: Mainnet vote 2025-09-03 17:00 UTC. Trap is wrong CAP/version.
Also good if the answer: Notes this is part of the SDF 'Road to 5000 TPS' scaling effort (parallel core / dissemination work). | Notes Whisk activated on Mainnet 2025-09-03.
Golden cites: The Protocol 23 / Whisk material and/or CAP-0063, plus the 'Parallelizing Stellar Core' blog.
GT-25/GT-31/GT-33: P23 support initialized setting one; setting-two activation was independently dated to 2026-01-29. Canonical SLP path is limits/slp-0004.md.
AUDIT 2026-11-02: SLP-0007 (limits/slp-0007.md) raised the setting from 2 to 3 at ledger 65080525 (2026-10-22 17:00 UTC). The current value is a volatile network setting; an undated claim that it is still 2 is stale.
